$comment: THE PROVIDER SETS, AND WHICH ONE IS DEFAULT. Selecting a set is a LOOKUP, never a branch: an engine naming its sets in a case statement would make adding a third one an engine change — the same defect removed from ladders one layer down. EPAM_PROVIDER_SET picks a key from `sets`; unset picks `defaultSet`. An unknown name is an ERROR listing the declared sets, never a silent fall-through, because falling back would run a whole programme on the wrong stack while looking configured.
$hotSwap: If one provider's tokens run out mid-programme, the other must be back on the air in SECONDS: one env var, no build, no test run, no git operation, no file copied over another. Both sets live on disk permanently and side by side, so an interrupted swap leaves no half-written state.

projectEnv.$comment: HOW A PROJECT'S ENV IS SPLIT. `base` holds what is true of the project whatever stack it runs on; `overlay` holds the provider-dependent half and is chosen by the active set — {set} is replaced by that set's projectEnvSuffix. Declared here so no script contains either filename as a literal: renaming them is a config edit.
projectEnv.$disjoint: base and overlay MUST NOT declare the same key. Disjoint files make load order irrelevant, so no caller has to know which wins — and a test asserts it rather than a comment claiming it.

openrouter.description: The stack in production today: OpenRouter and MiniMax, through the ai-run/AgentRunner path.
openrouter.$credentials: The two vendors this stack actually calls. Required, because a run that starts without them dies at the first seam instead of at the launcher.

balanceProbe._why: Pre-flight reports credits minus usage and refuses a launch the balance cannot cover (costControls.runBudgetUsd). regintel 20260919T224649Z resume 6 burned attempts into 402s; 2026-09-20 a launch was about to start on $13.50 for a ~$20 run.

codemie.description: Claude via the CodeMie SSO proxy, through the codemie-claude wrapper. Declared 2026-08-25 once its ladders existed — an undeclared set fails loudly, an empty one silently.
codemie.$credentials: NONE. The codemie-claude wrapper authenticates through CodeMie SSO; no key reaches this layer.

mockserver.description: Claude Code answered by MockServer over HTTP. No credentials, no spend. Named for the MECHANISM: 'mock' collides with the ordinary word this repo uses throughout, and 'replay' is already a PROVIDER — the cassette rehearsal in ai-run.sh, which replays at the ai-run layer and therefore cannot reach Claude Code at all. Different mechanism, different layer, different name.
mockserver.$credentials: NONE. MockServer answers over plain HTTP. A free rehearsal that can reach a paid vendor is not a free rehearsal.

claude.description: Plain Claude Code on the operator's own tokens. The default stack.
claude.$credentials: NONE, DELIBERATELY. Claude Code authenticates through the OAuth session on disk. An ANTHROPIC_API_KEY present in the environment OUTRANKS that session, so exporting one here would bill an API account while the subscription the operator pays for went unused - which is exactly what happened for seven runs.

copilot.description: GitHub Copilot CLI (`copilot`) on the operator's own GitHub account. Climbs the claude set's ladders; each model is mapped to the id Copilot serves at call time.
copilot.$credentials: THE ACCOUNT IS PINNED, NOT WHICHEVER ONE `copilot` LAST USED. ~/.copilot can hold several logins (the operator's personal account and a client-provisioned EMU account); COPILOT_GITHUB_TOKEN outranks them all, so a run bills exactly the account whose token the install's .env carries. Operator, 2026-09-27: the personal account.

redirect.$why: How a rehearsal points this set at a stand-in model, declared rather than known by any harness: the Copilot CLI's own BYOK redirect (COPILOT_PROVIDER_BASE_URL, an OpenAI-compatible endpoint), offline so it makes no GitHub call (without COPILOT_OFFLINE a BYOK session hangs after its result, 2026-09-27).

codemie-web.description: CodeMie web assistants (the operator's own CodeMie account): every pipeline agent is a stored assistant named 'Pipeline <codeline> <agent>', reaching the codeline through a local CodeMie Plugin. Climbs the claude set's ladders.
codemie-web.$credentials: NONE at this layer. Calls ride the CodeMie CLI's SSO login (the same client mx-tracker uses); plugin keys are minted and registered by the set's own runner, kept in the install, never in .env templates.

signInProbe._why: Pre-flight runs it (path relative to orchestrations/). A signed-out CodeMie session, a ladder model missing from CodeMie's catalog, or a missing codemie-plugins environment fails every rung of every story mid-run; this refuses the launch instead.

pythonEnv._why: The local CodeMie Plugin a codemie-web agent reaches the codeline through (lib/codemie-web/plugins.js). The installer provisions it (python3 -m venv + pip, path relative to the install root); the runner reads the path from here. Pinned: 0.2.0 is the version proven 2026-09-28.

redirect.$why: How a rehearsal points this set at CodeMie stood in for, declared rather than known by any harness: the runner's CodeMie API (EPAM_CODEMIE_WEB_URL — a plain SDK client, no SSO) and the plugin engine its local plugins connect to (EPAM_CODEMIE_PLUGIN_ENGINE_URI).

$defaultSet: Chosen by the operator 2026-08-25. codemie is what RUNS; openrouter is the hot-swap target kept fully executable beside it. This field previously read 'openrouter' — a value nobody chose: it was invented when this registry was written and then read back as if it were a requirement.

freeRunCredentials.$comment: A free run scrubs every credential-shaped variable so it CANNOT authenticate to a paid LLM API. Some credentials are not LLM credentials and must survive, or the run fails for the wrong reason: scrubbing JIRA_TOKEN made Jira ingest return 0 issues and phase 'core' aborted, which looked like a pipeline defect and was a guard defect.
freeRunCredentials.$why: Declared here rather than hardcoded in free-run-guard.sh: which services are free is a fact about a deployment, not about the engine. A new non-LLM service is a config edit.

$spendProbeWhy: A run reported its spend by curling a vendor credit endpoint hardcoded in ten places across six launchers, guarded only by `[ -n $OPENROUTER_API_KEY ]`. So a codemie or mockserver run still called OpenRouter — on a free run, the one vendor call that was supposed to be impossible. Which endpoint reports credit is a fact about a STACK, so the set declares it. A set that declares none simply reports no spend.
$defaultSetWhy: claude is the default because CodeMie tokens are limited and cannot be topped up. codemie is hot swap 1, openrouter hot swap 2 — both remain declared and unchanged, and swapping is EPAM_PROVIDER_SET, not an edit.
$credentials: WHICH CREDENTIALS A STACK NEEDS IS A FACT ABOUT THE STACK, so it is declared here and nowhere else. orchestrate.sh exported EPAM_API_KEY_MINIMAX and EPAM_API_KEY_OPENROUTER on EVERY stack, and a project's REQUIRED_KEYS named those same two vendors - so a project pinned to claude could not launch without keys for a stack it never calls, and every run carried usable credentials for vendors it was not using. Each entry maps the source variable the operator sets (`from`) to the name the pipeline reads (`env`); `required` means the launcher refuses rather than failing at the first seam. A project declares only what is true of it on ANY stack, such as a Jira token.
